2609.26527.title: A Semiotics-Aware Framework for Evaluating Fidelity and Coverage in Natural Language Generation
2609.26527.paper_summary: When two texts describe the same expression, standard metrics based on lexical overlap or whole-text similarity may fail to detect meaningful differences in how that expression is framed. We propose a framework to evaluate semiotic alignment between texts, where a semiotic profile encompasses both the contextual meaning and the discourse references made salient by a text. Our approach yields two scores, Semiotic Fidelity and Semiotic Coverage, estimating how much of one text's profile is supported by the other and how much of the other's profile it recovers. Experiments show that coverage is typically lower than fidelity, and that alignment between LLMs and human-curated data is highest at low sampling temperatures, while higher temperatures reduce this alignment.
2609.26527.paper_summary_zh: 當兩個文本描述相同的表達時，基於詞彙重疊或整體文本相似性的標準指標可能無法檢測到該表達在框架上的有意義差異。我們提出了一個框架來評估文本之間的符號對齊，其中一個符號檔案包含文本所突顯的上下文意義和話語參考。我們的方法產生兩個分數，符號忠誠度和符號覆蓋率，估計一個文本的檔案有多少受到另一個文本的支持，以及另一個文本的檔案有多少被恢復。實驗顯示，覆蓋率通常低於忠誠度，並且大型語言模型（LLMs）與人類策劃數據之間的對齊在低取樣溫度下最高，而較高的溫度則降低了這種對齊。
2609.26527.author: Lorenzo Zangari et.al.
